title: Give every Michael feeder one harness that owns the ET window, the single-flight guard and the run row
user_role: Michael feeder process fired by Windows Task Scheduler or GitHub Actions
user_want: lib/michael/feeder.mjs to export runFeeder({ feeder, venue, window, upstream, run }, { sb, env, now, logger }) plus the pure assembleReadiness({ runs, now }) predicate, and lib/michael/rules-match.mjs to export matchGmailRule, matchKeywordBuckets and roleTagFor
user_benefit: So that each of the five feeders carries only its own domain logic, every fire outside its ET window is inert instead of wrong, a second fire fifteen minutes later cannot double-run the first, and the michael_feeder_runs row is written the same way by every venue.
criterion: Shared feeder harness lib/michael/feeder.mjs and pure rules matcher lib/michael/rules-match.mjs (PR 1)

ac.scenario: Off-window fire is inert, not an error
ac.given: the harness is invoked for feeder 'calendar-read' with window 04:00-05:00 ET and now is 07:12 ET
ac.then: it returns { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'outside_et_window' }, exits 0, writes no michael_feeder_runs row and makes no API call

ac.scenario: Unapplied child B migration is inert with zero writes
ac.given: michael_feeder_runs does not exist (PostgREST PGRST205 / Postgres 42P01) because the child B migration is unapplied
ac.when: runFeeder pre-flights the table through readRows
ac.then: it returns { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'tables_absent' }, never throws and performs no write

ac.scenario: Single-flight blocks a re-fire and a completed day
ac.given: a row for (feeder, et_date) has started_at set, finished_at null and started_at younger than ten minutes
ac.when: the next fifteen-minute fire calls runFeeder
ac.then: the fire is inert with reason 'in_flight'; an existing status ok row instead yields reason 'already_ok', while a degraded or failed row allows the retry to proceed

ac.scenario: Attempt numbering survives the unique-index race and upstream gating holds
ac.given: two fires race so the unique index rejects the second insert with 23505, and separately an upstream of [{ feeder, accept:['ok','degraded'] }] is unmet for today
ac.when: runFeeder computes attempt = max(attempt)+1 and checks upstream
ac.then: it retries the conflict exactly once before returning failed, and the unmet upstream yields inert with reason 'upstream_not_ready'

ac.scenario: Logs carry counts only and readiness degrades on time
ac.given: a feeder run that touched Gmail threads and calendar events, and a set of runs missing gmail at 05:45 ET
ac.when: log lines are captured and assembleReadiness({ runs, now }) is evaluated
ac.then: every '[michael:<feeder>] {...}' line is single-line JSON of counts and ids with no '@' and no thread subject text, and readiness waits until calendar is ok and gmail/todoist are ok-or-degraded, proceeding degraded at or after 05:45 ET with headsUp naming the missing feeders

ctx_intro:
Create lib/michael/feeder.mjs and lib/michael/rules-match.mjs. This is PR 1 and every other story in this SD imports it, so it lands first.

Move hhmmToMinutes and inWindow OUT of scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs:35-46 into feeder.mjs and re-import them in the tick. Do not leave a third copy; the tick's 62 existing tests must stay green as the proof the move was faithful.

runFeeder signature is fixed by VALIDATION c26274e9 condition 3: every feeder is `export async function runX({ sb, argv, now, ...deps })` with a private main(). Do NOT export main(argv, deps).

The harness owns, in order: window check, tables_absent pre-flight through lib/michael/db.mjs readRows, single-flight lookup, upstream check, start-row write (started_at), the caller's run(), then the completion write (finished_at, status ok|degraded|failed|skipped, counts, log_md of counts and ids only), and gracefulExit for the Task Scheduler venue. model_used/tokens_in/tokens_out stay null for the task_scheduler and gha venues; only the seat venue fills them (US-009).

A coded throw out of getAuthenticatedClient (HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED, MICHAEL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_MISSING, NO_STORED_TOKENS, invalid_grant) maps to status failed with counts.error_code, never to an uncaught exception.

rules-match.mjs is pure: matchGmailRule(rule_json, thread) over from/subject/list-id/label predicates (case-insensitive, all-of semantics), matchKeywordBuckets(rule_json, text) for the tasks four-bucket routing, and roleTagFor(rules, task) for todoist. Each returns { matched, rule_key } or null. No I/O, no clock, no env.

title: Read the chairman's two calendars at 04:00 ET and classify the day before he wakes
user_role: Chairman as host operator whose day shape is decided by his calendar
user_want: scripts/michael/calendar-read.mjs to run under the harness in the 04:00-05:00 ET window, upsert michael_calendar_day for today plus and minus one ET day across 'primary' and MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID, and classify today as Recovery, Interpersonal, Deep or Shallow
user_benefit: So that the morning brief opens with the true shape of the day, including coded events, optional meetings and overlapping blocks, without the chairman reading two calendars himself.

ac.scenario: Three ET dates upsert on the natural key
ac.given: fixture events spanning yesterday, today and tomorrow on both calendars
ac.then: michael_calendar_day is upserted by (et_date, event_id) with calendar_id, title, starts_at, ends_at, all_day, response_status, coded_marker, optional and overlap_group, and a re-run produces no duplicate rows

ac.scenario: Coded, optional and overlap derivations are exact
ac.given: a title carrying a leading bracket tag such as [DEEP] or [OFFICE], an event with needsAction or tentative response or 'optional' in the title, and two events on one date whose intervals intersect
ac.then: coded_marker holds the bracket tag, optional is true for the optional cases, and the intersecting events share one overlap_group id

ac.scenario: Every classification branch is reachable
ac.given: fixtures for no non-optional events, three or more accepted meetings, a coded [DEEP] event, fewer than two meetings, and a Tuesday with an accepted in-office event
ac.when: today is classified into the run row counts
ac.then: the results are Recovery, Interpersonal, Deep, Deep and Interpersonal respectively, with the coded-event override winning over the meeting count and the Tuesday-office rule applied

ac.scenario: One calendar down degrades, both down fails
ac.given: the Exelon calendar rejects while 'primary' succeeds
ac.then: status is degraded with counts.failed_calendar naming it; when both reject the status is failed

ac.scenario: The wrong venue and the wrong hour do nothing
ac.given: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, and separately a fire at 07:12 ET
ac.then: the first is failed with counts.error_code HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED and no API call, and the second exits 0 inert with reason 'outside_et_window' and no API call

ctx_intro:
Create scripts/michael/calendar-read.mjs exporting runCalendarRead({ sb, argv, now, auth, calendar }) and a private main(). It runs under runFeeder with feeder id 'calendar-read', venue 'task_scheduler', window 04:00-05:00 ET and no upstream dependency.

Read events.list for today plus and minus one ET day on both 'primary' and MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID through listCalendarEvents from US-002. Upsert michael_calendar_day by the natural key (et_date, event_id).

Classification for today, written into the run row counts as { classification, events_by_date, coded, optional, overlaps }:
- Recovery when there are no non-optional events
- Interpersonal when there are three or more accepted meetings
- Deep when a coded [DEEP] event exists, or when there are fewer than two meetings
- Shallow otherwise
The coded-event override wins over the meeting count. The Tuesday-office rule marks a Tuesday Interpersonal when any accepted in-office event exists.

title: Act on the recorded intents under a modify ceiling that a killed run can resume without repeating
user_role: Chairman as host operator who needs the inbox actually moved, but bounded
user_want: gmail-triage --apply to walk the item rows that carry action_intent with no action_taken_at, call modifyThread in creation order, stamp action_taken_at, and stop at MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING
user_benefit: So that a rules mistake can move at most sixty threads in one night, an interrupted run resumes exactly where it stopped instead of double-archiving, and a thread the chairman pulled back into the inbox is flagged rather than silently archived again.
criterion: gmail-triage part 2: record-then-act with the modify ceiling and borderline resurfacing (PR 4b)

ac.scenario: The ceiling stops the run and leaves the remainder
ac.given: 80 seeded matched threads carrying action_intent and a ceiling of 60
ac.then: exactly 60 modifyThread calls are made, status is degraded with counts.ceiling_hit true and counts.threads_modified 60, and the remaining 20 rows keep action_intent with no action_taken_at for the next run or the seat

ac.scenario: An interrupted run resumes without repeating
ac.given: a run was killed after 30 modifies had stamped action_taken_at
ac.when: the script is re-run on the same rows
ac.then: it makes exactly the remaining modify calls and none of the first 30, which is the record-then-act idempotency of spec section 5 and the section 11 test

ac.scenario: A resurfaced thread is flagged, never re-archived
ac.given: an earlier row with action_intent archive and action_taken_at set, whose thread is back in the inbox with a newer last_message_id
ac.then: the row is written borderline true with class kept and no automatic action is taken on it

ac.scenario: One modify failure does not stop the others
ac.given: the Gmail modify call rejects for a single thread
ac.when: the run continues through the remaining intents
ac.then: that row is left without action_taken_at, counts.modify_failed is 1, and the run completes rather than aborting

ac.scenario: Failed means genuinely failed
ac.given: every modify call rejects, or the API is unreachable
ac.then: status is failed; any outcome where at least one modify succeeded is ok or degraded, never failed

ctx_intro:
Extend scripts/michael/gmail-triage.mjs from US-004 with the --apply path. The read-only recording from PR 4a is unchanged; this PR only adds the act leg, which is why the ordering matters and why US-004 ships the APPLY_NOT_LANDED refusal that this story removes.

**Record-then-act** is the whole design (spec section 5 and the section 11 idempotency test). The row is written first with action_intent and no action_taken_at. --apply then walks rows with action_intent and no action_taken_at, in creation order, calls modifyThread from lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs (TRASH and SPAM are already refused there by child C), and stamps action_taken_at per thread. A killed run re-executed therefore acts only on what it had not yet stamped.

**The ceiling** is MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING, default 60, from lib/michael/constants.mjs. When the count would exceed it, stop applying, mark the run degraded with counts.ceiling_hit true, and leave the remaining intents in place for the next run or the seat.

**Borderline resurfacing**: a thread with an earlier row carrying action_intent archive and action_taken_at set, which reappears in the inbox with a newer last_message_id, is written borderline true with class kept and is NOT modified. The chairman pulled it back; the feeder does not overrule him.

title: Route the Google Tasks export into four buckets and stage the cleanup instead of writing back to Drive
user_role: Chairman as host operator whose captured tasks arrive as a Drive export
user_want: scripts/michael/tasks-classifier.mjs to run in the 03:45-04:30 ET window, read current-tasks.json from MICHAEL_TASKS_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID, route each item through matchKeywordBuckets, create deduped Todoist tasks, and stage the consumed set rather than writing it back
user_benefit: So that captured tasks land in the right Todoist project with both labels and without duplicates, and so the v1 read-only Drive grant is respected instead of being quietly assumed to allow writes.

ac.given: current-tasks.json has a modifiedTime older than 36 hours
ac.then: the run is skipped with counts.reason 'stale' and no Todoist call is made

ac.scenario: An unconsumed cleanup blocks the next pass
ac.given: a cleanup-pending.json exists in the folder newer than the last consumed marker recorded in the last ok run's counts
ac.then: the run is skipped with counts.reason 'cleanup_pending' and nothing is created

ac.scenario: Four-bucket routing and staging of the remainder
ac.given: active michael_rules domain tasks whose rule_json names the bucket and target Todoist project and label, plus items no rule routes
ac.when: each item is passed through matchKeywordBuckets
ac.then: routed items go to their bucket's project and carry both labels, and unrouted items are staged to michael_staged_items kind 'task_route' for the seat's grading

ac.given: a seeded Todoist task created in the last 7 days with the captured label and from-google-tasks, matching an export item on normalized content
ac.then: no task is created for it

ac.scenario: Cleanup is staged and the venue is enforced
ac.given: the v1 grant is drive.readonly, and separately GITHUB_ACTIONS=true
ac.when: the consumed set is handled, and when the script runs in Actions
ac.then: the cleanup list is staged to michael_staged_items kind 'tasks_cleanup' with the file ids and counts.cleanup_staged is recorded with no Drive write, and the Actions run is failed with error_code HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED and no Drive call

ctx_intro:
Create scripts/michael/tasks-classifier.mjs exporting runTasksClassifier({ sb, argv, now, auth, drive, todoist }) and a private main(). It runs under runFeeder with feeder id 'tasks-classifier', venue 'task_scheduler', window 03:45-04:30 ET and no upstream dependency. It is the earliest host feeder of the night.

Read current-tasks.json from MICHAEL_TASKS_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID through readDriveFileText (US-002). Two guard conditions come before any work: a modifiedTime older than 36 hours aborts skipped with counts.reason 'stale'; a cleanup-pending.json in the folder newer than the last consumed marker (recorded in the counts of the last ok run) aborts skipped with counts.reason 'cleanup_pending'.

Routing uses matchKeywordBuckets (US-001) against active michael_rules domain tasks, where rule_json names the bucket and the target Todoist project and label. Items no rule routes are staged to michael_staged_items kind 'task_route' for the seat.

Dedupe before creating: fetch Todoist tasks with the captured label and from-google-tasks created in the last 7 days and compare normalized content. Created tasks carry both labels.

**The Drive write does not happen in v1.** The grant is drive.readonly, so the consumed set is staged to michael_staged_items kind 'tasks_cleanup' with the file ids and counts.cleanup_staged is recorded. The Apps Script consumer is explicitly out of scope for this SD.
